newsitem.title: UK: Big U.S. chemical firms see '97 sales up 4.4%.
newsitem.headline: Big U.S. chemical firms see '97 sales up 4.4%.

text.p: - The largest U.S. chemical companies with turnover of more than $1 billion expect sales to rise by an average of 4.4 percent this year, the president of the U.S. Chemical Manufacturers Association (CMA) said on Thursday.

Fred Webber told the business outlook conference of the UK's Chemical Industries Association that smaller companies, with sales of under $1 billion, are predicting stronger growth of around 5.0 percent.

But the U.S. industry expects to see strong profit growth this year despite relatively slow economic expansion as it reaps the benefit of lower raw material costs and the easing of other cost pressures.

Citing an annual CMA survey, Webber said smaller companies expected profits to advance by an average of 23.2 percent this year, while larger producers see "a much more modest but still impressive gain" of 9.7 percent. "1996 was a good year for the U.S. chemical industry and the prospects for 1997 also appear to be good," said Webber.
Neither sector sees any change from the pattern of wage rises in recent years, with larger companies forecasting 3.5 percent growth in wage bills this year and smaller businesses 3.3 percent.

While larger businesses predicted steady growth in research and development spending in the next two years of around three to four percent a year, smaller businesses see spending rising by between five and six percent this year and by four percent in 1998.
